identity.title: The ALMA Patchy Deep Survey: a blind search for [C II] emitters at z ∼ 4.5
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present a result of a blind search for [C II] 158 $\mu$m emitters at $z\sim 4.5$ using ALMA Cycle 0 archival data.

targets.name: 243 fields from 8 Cycle 0 projects (NGC1614, SBS0335-052, COSMOS, GRBs, NGC1097, NGC1433, ECDFS, VV114)

evidence.quote: The total number of fields is 243 and the total on-source exposure time is 19.2 hours.

question.value: Are there blindly detectable [C II] emitters at z~4.5 in ALMA Cycle 0 band 7 archival data, and what limits does this place on the [C II] luminosity function?

evidence.quote: In order to obtain better constraint to the [C II] luminosity function at $z>4$, we carried out a blind search for [C II] emitters at $z\sim 4.5$ using ALMA Cycle 0 archival data.
we searched Cycle 0 Projects covering $330-360$ GHz (in band 7)

frequencies_and_spectral_setup.value: 7.5 GHz FDM (0.98 MHz) or 8 GHz TDM (31.2 MHz) channels

evidence.quote: the data with 8 GHz bandwidth were taken with continuum mode (TDM mode, the spectral resolution is 31.2 MHz or $\sim$27 km s$^{-1}$)
the synthesised beam size ranges from $0''.4-3''.8$
The total on-source exposure time of the data is 19.2 hours.

what.value: [C II] line widths of 27 z>4 galaxies/QSOs used to choose spectral binning

evidence.quote: Figure 1 show a distribution of the [C II] velocity width (FWHM) of 27 [C II]-detected galaxies/QSOs at $z>4$
we plot the [C II] luminosity function expected from the $z\sim 4$ UV luminosity function from (cite: 2006ApJ...653..988Y)

what.value: SFR/L[CII] calibration log SFR = -8.52 + 1.18 log L[CII]

evidence.quote: log$SFR$(M$_{\ensuremath{\odot}}$ yr$^{-1}$) $=  -8.52 + 1.18\times$log$L_{\rm [C\,{\sevensize II}]} (L_{\odot})$, by (cite: 2014arXiv1402.4075D)

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: [C II] luminosity function at z=4 from numerical simulation

evidence.quote: We also compared with the [C II] luminosity function at $z=4$ predicted from a numerical simulation (cite: 2014PASJ...66...70O)

pipeline_or_manual.value: archive-provided calibration; phase calibrator checked with clean against calibrator database

evidence.quote: the derived flux density is consistent with the flux densities listed in the ALMA calibrator database

archive_products_used_as_is.value: archive calibrated data used, no re-calibration

evidence.quote: We used the calibrated data product provided by the archive, without any additional re-calibration of the data.
We used clean to construct data cubes with natural weighting to maximise the sensitivity.
We used clean to construct data cubes with natural weighting to maximise the sensitivity.
We adopted a pixel size of $0''.2$

continuum_subtraction.value: uvcontsub using line-free parts of the targets

evidence.quote: We used uvcontsub to subtract the continuum from the visibilities using line-free parts of the original targets with the multiple spectral windows.
we made data cubes with four different spectral resolutions (50, 100, 300, and 500 km s$^{-1}$)

what.value: Recalibrated data used by Swinbank et al. for the ECDFS SMG test

evidence.quote: Based on the data re-calibrated by (cite: 2013ApJ...768...91H), (cite: 2012MNRAS.427.1066S) detected the $z=4.4$ [C II] emission lines

unstated_but_needed: Exact line-free channel ranges for uvcontsub and continuum fit order
How candidate peaks were searched (peak finder, per-channel vs cube-wide) and how channels were binned
Survey-volume calculation details (primary beam cutoff, redshift coverage per field)
Treatment of channels excluded for high noise and original-target lines (which ones)

method.value: Searched Cycle 0 band 7 projects covering 330-360 GHz with published extragalactic results; used archive calibrated products

evidence.quote: We collected 8 extra-galactic projects from which initial results have been already published.

validation.value: Imaged phase calibrators to confirm flux and unresolved point-source

evidence.quote: We confirmed that the phase calibrator is detected as a spatially un-resolved source at the phase centre

method.value: uvcontsub then clean with natural weighting at four velocity resolutions

evidence.quote: We used clean to construct data cubes with natural weighting to maximise the sensitivity.
We adopted a pixel size of $0''.2$

method.value: Normalise flux by per-channel rms and search for peaks above 6 sigma; none found

evidence.quote: The flux is normalised by using the rms of each binned channel.
Therefore we set a threshold of 6-$\sigma$ for our line detection conservatively.
The overall shapes of the normalised flux distributions are well fitted with a Gaussian

validation.value: Recovered the two known z=4.4 SMG [C II] lines (ALESS 65.1 at 6.2 sigma, ALESS 61.1 at 3.8 sigma)

evidence.quote: we detected the emission line at 6.2-$\sigma$ from ALESS 65.1

method.value: Survey volume vs depth with primary beam correction; 1-sigma Poisson upper limits (Gehrels 1986); compare with UV-LF and simulation predictions

evidence.quote: The 1-$\sigma$ confidence upper limits on the space densities of [C II] emitters are calculated using Poisson statistics

assumptions.value: emitters spatially unresolved; A_UV=1; SFR=1.2e-28 L_UV; cosmology H0=72, Om=0.27, OL=0.73

evidence.quote: We assume that line emitters are spatially unresolved in the data cubes.
We used the ALMA data reduction package CASA
In this search, we could not detect any line emitters above the 6-$\sigma$ significance level.
we detected the emission line at 6.2-$\sigma$ from ALESS 65.1
$L_{\rm [C\,{\sevensize II}]} = 2.9 \pm 0.5 \times 10^{9} L_{\odot}$
If we adopt a detection threshold of 5.5-$\sigma$, we could detect 6 emitter candidates.

results_numeric.quantity: Upper limit on number density at L=1e9 Lsun, 300 km/s

findings_qualitative.value: Upper limits are at least 2 orders of magnitude above LFs expected from UV LF or simulations.

evidence.quote: These limits are at least 2 orders of magnitude larger than the [C II] luminosity functions expected from the $z \sim 4$ UV luminosity function or from numerical simulation.

claims.hypothesis: Blind [C II] emitters at z~4.5 can be found in Cycle 0 archival band 7 data
claims.experiment: Search of continuum-subtracted cubes at four velocity resolutions over 243 fields
claims.finding: Only upper limits on the [C II] LF at z~4.5 over 1e8-1e10 Lsun, too shallow to constrain models

evidence.quote: We could not detect any new line emitters above a 6-$\sigma$ significance level.

claims.hypothesis: Cycle 1+2 archival data could constrain the [C II] LF
claims.experiment: Extrapolation of depth/volume to future data
claims.finding: An ALMA Patchy Deep Survey is feasible

evidence.quote: we would be able to better constrain the [C II] luminosity function

why_this_method.value: Spectral binning chosen from observed [C II] widths of high-z sources (median ~300 km/s, 90% within 50-500)

evidence.quote: The 90 per cent of the sample are distributed in the range of $50-500$ km s$^{-1}$.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: 5.5 sigma threshold rejected as too aggressive given negative-tail noise

evidence.quote: the 5.5-$\sigma$ detection threshold may be too aggressive to detect real source.

limitations_admitted.value: Extended [C II] emitters much larger than the beam could be missed

evidence.quote: we potentially miss spatially extended [C II] emitter whose size is much larger than the synthesised beam size.

referee_caveats_inferred: Low completeness: no injection-recovery tests beyond two known sources
Other lines (CO, [O III]) could contaminate but candidates were not followed up
Highly heterogeneous data and beams without a systematic completeness correction

evidence.quote: before we downloaded the data from the archive

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: ~100s GB to ~1 TB of calibrated measurement sets for 8 projects
reproducibility.score_reason: Public data and simple procedure, but search algorithm and volume calculation details are missing.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Main result is a null detection with partial recipe; search and volume details unstated.

companion_papers.why: Earlier serendipitous [C II] detection in two z=4.4 SMGs, used as test
